newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks firm after volatile start.
newsitem.headline: French stocks firm after volatile start.

text.p: French shares resumed their firm tone on Thursday mid-morning, overcoming earlier volatility sparked by uncertainty over the government's tax and budgetary measures, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 19.55 points or 0.67 percent at 2,929.00 at 0905 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 16 at 2,933 from Wednesday's close.
The market drew support from Wall Street's strong rise overnight and dollar firmness.
LVMH gains 2.66 percent to 1,622 francs, boosted by news that British groups Guinness and Grand Met were open to proposals for bringing LVMH's drinks business into their planned merger.
Thomson-CSF gains 2.68 percent on hopes the on-off privatisation might be back on the agenda.
Eurotunnel adds 3.97 percent after French lawyer Sophie L'Helias, proxy-holder for institutional investors, said on Wednesday she would support the debt restructuring plan.
Usinor runs into profit-taking, down 1.44 percent at 102.5, after recent run up on the back of its entry into the CAC index on July 25.

Lyonnaise des Eaux/Suez falls 1.13 percent to 613. The group said it is holding its forecast of net attributable profit above 3.5 billion francs for 1997, saying the British government's windfall tax on utilities had been factored into the group forecast.
The utilities group holds a 70 percent stake in Britain's Northumbrian Water Group Plc, which must pay 79 million pounds in two tranches.
